cases.evidence: Boundary split a multiword institution name so the translator guessed the institution type; oracle shows the head 'Hospital' was needed.
cases.proposed_rule: If a candidate would cut a multiword proper name or institutional/place NP before its syntactic head (tokens like Hospital/Center/University/Institute/School/etc.), allow the candidate but enforce that it must not be ranked above any surrounding clause-completing or punctuation-adjacent candidate; i.e., treat such intra-name cuts as lower-priority until the head appears.

example_pair.input: He trained as an obstetrician and began to work at the Auckland's National Women's Hospital in 1959.
example_pair.output: He trained as an obstetrician <SEG:90> and began to work at the Auckland's National Women's Hospital <SEG:95> in 1959.

cases.span: the significance of the piece <SEG:30> of genetic material <SEG:65> affected
cases.evidence: Cut before the participial modifier 'affected' detached the adjective from its head and caused wrong attachment/scope in translation.
cases.proposed_rule: Do not allow a candidate that finalizes a predicate about entities when a following modifier or classifier (participial adjective, relative clause, or noun post-modifier like 'affected', 'damaged', 'classified') remains inside the same NP; such candidates must be scored below the next clause- or punctuation-completing candidate.

example_pair.input: Mutations can have a variety of different effects depending on the type of mutation, the significance of the piece of genetic material affected and whether the cells affected are germ-line cells.
example_pair.output: Mutations can have a variety of different effects <SEG:85> depending on the type of mutation, <SEG:50> the significance of the piece of genetic material affected <SEG:80> and whether the cells affected are germ-line cells.

cases.span: it has been for sealers <SEG:80> in the past 15 years
cases.evidence: Boundary left the noun 'sealers' to be resolved without its domain phrase; translator chose wrong sense ('sealers'→'封印者').
cases.proposed_rule: If a common noun's sense is plausibly disambiguated by an immediately following domain/PP or time-phrase (e.g., 'for X', 'in Y years'), ensure any candidate that would force a standalone translation of that noun is ranked below clause-completing or disambiguating candidates so the disambiguator is visible before finalizing sense.

example_pair.input: The amount and thickness of the pack ice, according to Pittman, is the worst it has been for sealers in the past 15 years.
example_pair.output: The amount and thickness of the pack ice, according to Pittman, <SEG:80> is the worst it has been for sealers in the past 15 years <SEG:95>.

cases.span: once an agreement is signed <SEG:55> while the PA agrees <SEG:50>
cases.evidence: Cut before connective/clause attachment completed: translator incorrectly attached duration to the wrong party because 'only for five years' came later.
cases.proposed_rule: When a temporal/connective marker (once/while/after/before) appears and its attachment will be resolved by the following clause (who does what for how long), do not let an interior candidate outrank the full connective+clause boundary; treat such connective-adjacent candidates as lower priority than the clause they introduce.

example_pair.input: Israel demands an ongoing military presence in the valley for ten years once an agreement is signed while the PA agrees to leave such presence only for five years.
example_pair.output: Israel demands an ongoing military presence in the valley for ten years <SEG:80> once an agreement is signed <SEG:55> while the PA agrees to leave such presence only for five years <SEG:90>.

cases.span: To finish, Turkish <SEG:40> dance group Fire of Anatolia performed <SEG:90> the show "Troy"
cases.evidence: Cut before object clarified the performance type; translator chose a verb sense ('played' music) inconsistent with the following object 'the show "Troy"'.
cases.proposed_rule: If a general action verb (perform/do/hold/play) is followed by an object that determines the sub-type of performance (show/concert/lecture), ensure any candidate that would force choosing a language-specific verb sense is ranked below the object-completing boundary so the object is visible before committing the verb translation.

example_pair.input: To finish, Turkish dance group Fire of Anatolia performed the show "Troy".
example_pair.output: To finish, Turkish dance group Fire of Anatolia <SEG:60> performed the show "Troy" <SEG:90>.

cases.span: and many of the smaller pyramids, <SEG:80> tombs, and temples <SEG:80> were built to <SEG:20> honor Khufu's wives
cases.evidence: Boundary emitted a noun-list fragment that the remaining predicate ('were built') actually licenses; translator rendered the fragment as an independent assertion.
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid marking-and-high-scoring boundaries that leave a nominal list without its governing predicate; if the main predicate for a preceding NP has not yet appeared, keep such NP-internal candidates lower in rank than the predicate-completing boundary.

example_pair.input: The great pyramid was created to honor the Pharaoh Khufu, and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples were built to honor Khufu's wives and family members.
example_pair.output: The great pyramid was created <SEG:90> to honor the Pharaoh Khufu, <SEG:85> and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples <SEG:60> were built to honor Khufu's wives and family members <SEG:95>.

summary: The prompt is generous about candidacy but lacks relative-ranking constraints that keep clause-completing, punctuation-adjacent, or disambiguating boundaries above risky interior cuts. Many errors come from finalizing heads, predicates, or noun senses before disambiguating tokens arrive; the fix is to enforce that intra-NP/head or verb–object candidates never outrank the surrounding clause/punctuation-completing candidates rather than simply banning or globally downscoring them.

aggregate.dominant_basis: No corpus rate identifies a dominant failure. Read the cases and `judge_distribution` for WHICH mechanism to fix — do not infer a rate from `case_label_counts`, those cases were selected for being the worst.

coverage.of: all sentences scored — a true corpus rate
coverage.meaning: sentences where the tightest budget asked for boundaries the prompt never marked, so pieces are missing outright

premature_among_judged.of: boundaries judged this iteration, selected as the WORST by measured contradiction — NOT a corpus rate, do not compare it against `coverage`

case_label_counts.of: the selected worst cases — NOT a rate
